title: HDDS-13128. Expose per DN space utilisation as JMX metrics
description:
## What changes were proposed in this pull request?

Currently there are no node-level aggregated DN JMX metrics available to track the space utilised on a Datanode across all its volumes. Having JMX metrics to track the space utilisation per Datanode, allows monitoring and enables the user to take action when the space utilized on a DN is high, by adding nodes or running the Container Balancer.
A new class `DatanodeStorageMetrics` is added to expose 3 metrics related to space utilisation: `Capacity`, `Used` and `UsedPercentage`.

## What is the link to the Apache JIRA
https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HDDS-13128

## How was this patch tested?
1. Resulting JMX Metrics:
```json
{
    "name" : "Hadoop:service=HddsDatanode,name=DatanodeStorageMetrics",
    "modelerType" : "DatanodeStorageMetrics",
    "tag.Context" : "ozone",
    "tag.Hostname" : "7d739934c5d0",
    "OzoneCapacity" : 105076655700,
    "OzoneUsed" : 4382720,
    "OzoneUsedPercentage" : 0.004170974010167322
}
```
2. Newly added Unit Tests.

bugs.summary: DatanodeStorageMetrics.getMetrics() reads the totals through MutableVolumeSet.getStorageReport(), which takes the volume-set read lock. The metrics system calls getMetrics() while holding the DefaultMetricsSystem monitor, and MutableVolumeSet.failVolume() holds the volume-set write lock while HddsVolume.failVolume() unregisters VolumeIOStats, which needs that same monitor. The opposite lock orders deadlock the metrics thread and the volume-failure handler, after which every metrics register, unregister or sample in the process blocks.
bugs.trigger: A metrics sample (JMX/Prometheus sink timer) of DatanodeStorageMetrics runs while another thread holds the volume-set write lock, e.g. during failVolume() when a data volume fails: the sampler waits for the read lock while holding the metrics-system monitor that failVolume() needs.
